# Buffered physical responses: finite alternative, affine nullity, and a free-facet obstruction

This note retains the invariant energy buffer, actual compatible body speeds,
and the exact finite-contact continuation. It proves an exact separation
interface and one conditional geometric obstruction to its dual. It does not
prove that the dual is impossible for arbitrary compatible fibers, and it does
not prove OC. In particular, the separation theorem alone is a reformulation
of the remaining payment problem.

Dependencies:

* `candidate c6bafe9ff5de0861`;
* `candidate 86dd5366456916a8`,
  especially Sections 6, 11, and 13;
* `candidate 85a041ec649c5375`
  for a proved class of physically realizable response cones.

## 1. The exact finite linear response list

Use the continuation source's notation: N=d+1, total volume M, level
Q=beta M, within-fiber covariance Sigma, Gamma(u)^2=u^T Sigma u, and
f=(E/M)^(1/N). For each covering group i, Gamma(u_ij)=1,

    sum_j rho_ij=1,
    B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij,
    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/B_i,
    delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i.

All rho and coareas S are positive. The finite old contact set has bases
J_i, common energy E_i, and unique interior marks y_z. Every selected
cap is regular in the sense required for the joint threshold/shape
expansion in the continuation source.

For an ACTUAL bounded signed inward speed array v, put

    D(v)=sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) v_z,
    L_ij(v)=actual fixed-cap loss,
    C_z(v)=integral_boundary(K_z) [1+a_z.(X-y_z)]^(-N) v_z,
    Q_i,z(X)=sum_j rho_ij [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2,
    J_i(v)=sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) Q_i,z(X) v_z.

Here a_z is the own energy minimizer, g_z is the ordinary centroid, and
all integrals use the ORIGINAL bodies and original normal speeds. Define
one linear functional for every pair (i,z), z in J_i:

    Lambda_iz(v)
      =sum_j theta_ij L_ij(v)
       +delta_i C_z(v)/(N E_i)
       +delta_i J_i(v)/(2M)
       -[beta+delta_i(N+2)/(2NM)]D(v).                 (1)

The exact continuation theorem says that the covering response for group i
has negative normalized derivative precisely when

    min_(z in J_i) Lambda_iz(v)>0.                    (2)

Thus positivity of EVERY member of the finite list (1) is sufficient for
an actual strict decrease of the global normalized buffered maximum.
There is no selection of a favorable contact point in (1).

## 2. Finite separation has no hidden closed-cone assumption

Let R be a convex cone of vectors (Lambda_iz(v)) in R^m, where m is the
number of pairs (i,z). Assume every vector of R used below is the first
response of an actual admissible path. Such a cone is supplied by finite
global-cut speed addition, under the regularity hypotheses above. Other
classes require their own physical closure proof; arbitrary Minkowski
interpolation does not supply it.

Exactly one of the following alternatives holds:

(A) some r in R has all m coordinates strictly positive;

(B) there are eta_iz>=0, sum eta_iz=1, such that

    sum_(i,z) eta_iz Lambda_iz(v)<=0                  (3)

for every response in R.

Indeed, separate R from the OPEN positive orthant if they are disjoint.
Because R is a cone containing zero, the separating constant is zero.
The separator must be nonnegative coordinatewise: otherwise letting that
positive-orthant coordinate tend to infinity violates separation. It is
nonzero and can be normalized to sum one. Conversely (3) excludes (A).
This argument does not assert or need topological closedness of R.

For a specified finite library of k physically addable actions, (A) is the
linear feasibility problem Ht>0, t>=0, where H records their responses.
Its dual is eta>=0, sum eta=1, H^T eta<=0. A successful response can be
formed from at most m library actions by conic Caratheodory. No assertion
that a convenient finite library exhausts the physical cone is made.

## 3. Regular singleton groups and their exact dual boundary density

If each group has a positive-weight base-regular selected cap, Section 13
of the buffered source gives J_i={p_i}. The number of groups can then be
chosen at most k(P), and at most 2^n. Write y_i,a_i for the own mark and
energy parameter. For a dual eta_i as in (3), its boundary density is

    Xi_z(X)=sum_i eta_i {
        W_i(z,X)-beta
        +delta_i [ 1_(z=p_i) L_i(X)^(-N)/(N E_i)
                   +Q_i,z(X)/(2M)-(N+2)/(2NM) ] },      (4)

where W_i is the ACTUAL weighted fixed-cap inward-loss selector
sum_j theta_ij kappa_ij. Then the left side of (3) is exactly

    sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) Xi_z(X) v_z(X).        (5)

The regular cap assumptions make the selectors unambiguous surface-a.e.
There is no arbitrary allocation on a positive-area supporting facet in
this version. Energy kernels and covariance weights are bounded on the
fixed compact boundaries. Thus (4) is a genuine finite signed measure,
not a formal expression involving undefined normal derivatives.

## 4. Every common fiber-affine motion is exactly null

Let an infinitesimal lattice-preserving fiber-affine motion be

    V_z(X)=A X+Bz+c,
    v_z(X)=-n_z(X).V_z(X).                             (6)

The actual maps X -> (I+tA)X+t(Bz+c) preserve all anchored inclusions
for both signs of small t. Set

    V_i=A y_i+Bp_i+c,
    R_i=sum_j rho_ij u_ij.A Sigma u_ij.

Then EACH regular singleton functional in (1) vanishes on (6).
This is stronger than a statement about a selected dual combination.

Here is the complete cancellation. The ordinary divergence theorem gives

    D=-M tr A.

For a proper cap, divergence on its captured part gives

    L_ij=-Q tr A-S_ij u_ij.(A bar X_ij+B bar z_ij+c).

The same formula applies to strict full/empty fibers after summation.
Regular normal stationarity gives

    bar z_ij=p_i,
    bar X_ij=y_i-epsilon f_i Sigma u_ij,
    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=epsilon f_i a_i.

Consequently

    sum_j theta_ij L_ij
      =-Q tr A-delta_i(a_i.V_i-R_i).                 (7)

Affine covariance of projective energy, differentiating at the fixed old
mark, gives

    C_pi/E_i=-tr A+N a_i.V_i.

Alternatively this follows directly by differentiating the projective
integral and using stationarity in its parameter. Differentiating the
centered second moments gives

    J_i=-M tr A-2M R_i.

Substitution in the correction part of (1) yields

    delta_i [ C_pi/(N E_i)+J_i/(2M)
                         -(N+2)D/(2NM) ]
       =delta_i(a_i.V_i-R_i).                       (8)

Equations (7)--(8), beta M=Q, and D=-M tr A prove Lambda_i(v)=0.
In particular the quadratic covariance term cancels the angular work R_i
exactly. Dropping it produces a spurious descent or obstruction under a
mere affine coordinate change. The calculation includes translations,
base-dependent shears, trace-free linear maps, and homotheties.

## 5. A conditional free-facet obstruction to the dual

Now suppose d>=2 and K_z is a polytope with a facet F of positive
(d-1)-measure. Impose the following PHYSICAL freedom hypotheses for the
cone against which (3) holds:

(i) both signs of the normal parallel motion of this facet, with all
other first boundary speeds zero, are feasible;

(ii) adding one outward point over p=centroid(F) is feasible, with first
inward speed -T_p on F and zero elsewhere, where T_p is the unit-height
pyramid tent on F with peak p and zero boundary values.

Strict anchored containment sufficient to perturb this fiber supplies
these freedoms; otherwise they are explicit additional hypotheses. The
standard finite-polytope geometry gives the stated first speeds: moving
one support plane has constant speed on its facet; a point at height t
over relint F gives the pyramid roof t T_p, and corrections near other
facets have O(t^2) volume. There is no claim that arbitrary contact-
constrained facets have these freedoms. It is enough that the cone
contain the three specified responses; it need not contain arbitrary
signed facet functions.

Assume also that every cap with eta_i theta_ij>0 has one constant inward-
loss selector on relint F, up to a surface-null set. In particular no such
proper cutting hyperplane crosses relint F. Thus W in (4) is constant
on F. The remaining Xi_z is a smooth convex function on F. Its tangential
Hessian is the restriction of

    Hess Xi_z(X)=sum_i eta_i delta_i {
      1_(z=p_i) (N+1)/E_i L_i(X)^(-N-2) a_i a_i^T
      +(1/M)sum_j rho_ij u_ij u_ij^T }.               (9)

Every coefficient is nonnegative.

The two signed parallel motions and (3) force integral_F Xi_z=0.
If Xi_z is nonaffine on F, strict Jensen gives Xi_z(p)<0. For 0<=s<=1,
convexity gives

    Xi_z(p+s(X-p)) <= s Xi_z(X)+(1-s)Xi_z(p).

The superlevel sets of T_p are p+s(F-p), with tent level 1-s. Layer
cake and a change of variables therefore yield

    integral_F T_p Xi_z
      =integral_0^1 s^(d-1) integral_F Xi_z(p+s(X-p)) dX ds
      <= |F| Xi_z(p)/[d(d+1)] <0.                   (10)

The outward tent has response -integral_F T_p Xi_z>0, contradicting (3).
Hence every permissible dual must have Xi_z affine on F. By (9), this
forces, for every eta_i>0 and every j,

    u_ij.w=0 for every tangent vector w to F.         (11)

Any source-energy normal a_i on this facet also has zero tangential
component. It already follows from the buffered balance if all u_ij
are perpendicular to F.

Consequently if each group available to a dual has two nonparallel
continuous normals, no dual can coexist with a free facet uncut by all
of its positively weighted caps. More generally (11) is the exact
necessary degeneracy. This is a genuine strict first-order obstruction:
it uses the new positive quadratic covariance term, not only the
formal separation theorem.

It does not prove a global bound. At a hard minimizing family the
facet may be coupled to other fibers, the dual caps may cross it, or
all positively weighted normal groups may be parallel to that facet.
Those alternatives are retained rather than silently excluded.

## 6. Calibration and scope

For a one-dimensional facet F=[-1,1], take Xi(x)=x^2-1/3. Its uniform
integral is zero, while the unit centered tent 1-|x| has

    integral_F (1-|x|) Xi(x) dx=-1/6.

This verifies the sign and strictness mechanism in (10); it is not
asserted to be a complete critical mixed-family dual certificate.

The finite alternative (Section 2) is an exact organizing interface,
not new numerical payment. Section 4 is a necessary invariance check.
Section 5 adds a bounded geometric exclusion with stated physical
freedom and signature hypotheses. No smoothing argument transfers
variational stationarity to regular families, and no assertion about
all minimizing families is made.
